articles.headline: Contract Year Dynamics and Equipment Evaluation for Hill at RCR
articles.dek: Austin Hill enters the final year of his current agreement as talks surrounding future equipment options continue to develop.
articles.body:
As the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series garage opens for the 2026 campaign, attention naturally drifts to the contractual status of several key competitors. Among them, Austin Hill finds himself in the final year of his current deal with Richard Childress Racing. Sources indicate the driver remains content as the season begins, even as discussions regarding future equipment options and landing spots for next year remain a frequent topic of conversation in the paddock.

Hill is far from the only competitor navigating a contract year. Veteran racers Ryan Sieg, Ryan Ellis, Parker Retzlaff, and Josh Williams all enter the season with their current agreements expiring at the end of 2026. Teams and management teams are monitoring the market closely, though no formal announcements regarding next season's rosters are expected until late spring at the earliest.

Meanwhile, internal pressure is evident at Jordan Anderson Racing, where Blaine Perkins and Daniel Dye both enter the final year of their current deals amidst mounting frustration regarding equipment performance. Team leadership faces the task of stabilizing morale as the thirty-three-race schedule gets underway at Daytona.

Silly season activity remains in its initial phases with teams strictly focused on the immediate operational hurdles of the season opener. Future movement will depend heavily on early race performance and manufacturer alignment as the year progresses.
articles.author: Marcy Teague

pullQuote.text: Everyone is evaluating where they stand before making any long-term commitments.

byNumbers.label: Final year of current contracts for multiple veterans

takeaways: Austin Hill is in the final year of his RCR contract.
Equipment talks for next season remain in the discussion stage.
extras.whatsNext: On-track results at Daytona will set the tone for early-season negotiations.

articles.headline: Love Leads Final Daytona Practice Prior to United Rentals 300
articles.dek: Richard Childress Racing shows early superspeedway speed as Jesse Love paces the preseason test at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.body:
Preseason preparations for the 2026 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series concluded with a single test session at Daytona International Speedway, where Jesse Love set the benchmark speed. Piloting the Richard Childress Racing entry, Love posted the fastest lap of the day to top the timing sheets ahead of the upcoming United Rentals 300.

Teammate Austin Hill closely followed in second place, giving Richard Childress Racing a sweep of the top two positions on the speed charts. The strong showing establishes the baseline expectations for the RCR superspeedway program as teams complete their final setup adjustments.

Rajah Caruth put JR Motorsports in the top three with the third-fastest lap of the session, while teammate Carson Kvapil followed in fourth. RSS Racing veteran Ryan Sieg rounded out the top five. A total of twenty drivers recorded representative lap times during the track activity, though teams varied their run plans and drafting programs throughout the day.

Behind the leaders, Ryan Ellis placed sixth for Young's Motorsports, with Sam Mayer seventh for Haas Factory Team. Blaine Perkins, Brandon Jones, and Brent Crews completed the top ten positions. The field now transitions from testing to the official race weekend schedule, culminating in Saturday's season opener.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

pullQuote.text: We ran through our checklist and learned what the car needed in traffic.

keyMoments.text: Jesse Love sets the fastest single-lap speed of the session.

byNumbers.label: Drivers logging registered speeds in the test

takeaways: RCR cars secure the top two spots on the speed chart.
Drafting packs remained cautious during the test.
extras.whatsNext: The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series opens the 2026 season with the United Rentals 300.

articles.headline: Preseason Assessment and Field Breakdown for the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series
articles.dek: An in-depth look at the title contenders, dark horses, and new pairings heading into the season opener at Daytona.
articles.body:
The 2026 season of the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series arrives with a packed garage and plenty of intrigue as teams prepare for the United Rentals 300 at Daytona International Speedway. Looking across the entry list, the hierarchy of the series begins to take shape through organizational strength and offseason alignment.

At the top of the expectations list sit the powerhouse operations. Richard Childress Racing brings Jesse Love and Austin Hill back into the fold, with Love pacing the recent Daytona test session by turning the fastest lap at the top of the pylon. Hill slotting in right behind him in second confirms the immediate speed of the RCR equipment package on superspeedways.

JR Motorsports fields a formidable four-car lineup featuring Rajah Caruth, Carson Kvapil, Sammy Smith, and Justin Allgaier. Caruth and Kvapil showed strong testing pace right out of the box, landing third and fourth respectively in the United Rentals 300 practice readout. Joe Gibbs Racing counters with Brandon Jones, Brent Crews, William Sawalich, and Taylor Gray, aiming to translate technical depth into consistent race-winning execution.

Mid-pack stability relies on veterans and determined single-car or smaller multi-car efforts. Ryan Sieg leads the RSS Racing charge in his contract year, joined by teammate Kyle Sieg. Ryan Ellis anchors Young's Motorsports, while Sam Mayer and Sheldon Creed lead the Haas Factory Team effort. These groups look to capitalize on attrition and strategy when the drafting packs sort themselves out under race conditions.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

pullQuote.text: The speed is there in the Richard Childress Chevrolets right off the truck.

takeaways: RCR showed dominant speed in preseason testing.
JRM fields four competitive cars for the opener.
extras.whatsNext: Teams complete final preparations for the season opener at Daytona.
